_README: PARAPHRASE FAMILIES — the generalization corpus for Bruce's semantic executive.
Every entry in a family means THE SAME THING to a human. Bruce must map all of them to the same
normalized objective. These strings are DATA and must never be referenced by production code: the
moment a module matches one of these phrasings, this corpus stops measuring understanding and starts
measuring memorization. tests/test_language_generalization.py enforces that with a grep.
The 'held_out' members are the real test. 'seed' members are the wordings someone might plausibly
have written a rule for; held_out are the ones nobody did. A family passes only if the held-out
wordings land on the same objective as the seeds.
objective.operation is an EXACT ToolBroker registry id. If a rename makes one of these ids stale, the
suite must fail loudly rather than silently testing nothing.

_why: Follow-ups that only mean something against live state. Each names the state it needs.
`accept` IS A SET, NOT A LOOSENING. Some turns have two equally correct readings and the model
picks between them non-deterministically: 'nah dont send that' is `decision_response`+decline on
one call and `cancellation` on the next. Both refuse, both block execution, and the goal-survival
difference between them is not something the student expressed. Asserting one exact mode would
test which coin the model flipped, so instead each case asserts the set of correct readings PLUS
the property that actually matters — `must_not_execute`, which is checked on every refusal and is
a STRICTER claim than the mode equality it replaces.

_why: Phrasings Bruce does NOT yet understand, kept as strict-xfail so they cannot be quietly
forgotten and cannot quietly start passing without someone noticing. Deleting a case Bruce
fails is how a suite stays green while the product stays broken.

cases.text: remind me i've got tutoring at four
cases.actual: reads as operation_family=remember (the memory family), so no calendar capability resolves
cases.why: 'remind me' is a reminder verb and reminder.create is not a live capability. The read is defensible — the student may want a reminder rather than a calendar block — and forcing it to calendar would be guessing at which of two real products they meant.
cases.fix: a live reminder capability, or a disambiguating question rather than silence

_why: Deictic language — 'that', 'this', 'it', 'that thing' — means nothing without a referent, and
everything with one. These cases assert BOTH directions, which is the whole point:
* with NO referent, Bruce must CLARIFY. Guessing which event 'that thing' means is how the
wrong calendar entry gets moved.
* with an inline reply or exactly ONE compatible open goal, Bruce must RESOLVE that goal.
And resolving the goal is enough. 'move that thing to friday' may legitimately return
target_goal_id=<the calendar goal> + requested_edit={date: friday} + proposed_operation_id=None:
the executive said which work and what change, and the backend derives calendar.update_event from
the selected goal plus the edit. Demanding an operation id from the executive here would be asking
understanding to do the runtime's job.
